[FEATURE: hr]
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic effect. Demand is heavily suppressed in the pre-dawn hours, reaching its lowest point around 4–5 a.m. (contribution ≈ −3.5 in log space). It then climbs sharply through the morning, peaks around the evening rush at roughly 5–6 p.m. (contribution ≈ +1), and falls back through the late evening. A secondary rise is visible around 8 a.m.
[IMPORTANCE] This is by far the most important feature, with a vertical range of about 4.5 log-units — more than four times larger than any other feature.

[FEATURE: temp]
[EFFECT] Temperature has a non-monotonic, inverted-U effect. Very cold conditions (normalised temp near 0, roughly below 5 °C) strongly suppress demand (down to about −0.8). Demand is boosted most at mild-to-warm temperatures around a normalised value of 0.5–0.6 (roughly 20–25 °C, contribution up to about +0.25–0.30). At the highest temperatures the effect turns negative again, suggesting very hot days slightly deter rentals.
[IMPORTANCE] The second most important feature, with a vertical range of about 1.1 log-units; a meaningful but clearly secondary driver compared to the hour of day.

[FEATURE: yr]
[EFFECT] Year acts as a step change: hours in 2011 receive a consistently negative contribution (around −0.25 to −0.30), while hours in 2012 receive a positive contribution (around +0.15 to +0.25), reflecting the system's overall growth between years.
[IMPORTANCE] A moderately important feature with a step size of roughly 0.5–0.6 log-units; ranked around fifth or sixth overall.

[FEATURE: mnth]
[EFFECT] Month has a broadly seasonal, non-monotonic shape. January (month 1) produces the most negative contributions (down to about −0.7), demand rises through spring and peaks across the summer months (roughly June–September, contributions around +0.1 to +0.25), then eases slightly in autumn and winter without returning to January lows.
[IMPORTANCE] A moderate feature with a vertical range of roughly 0.9 log-units; similar in magnitude to humidity, and ranked around fourth or fifth.

[FEATURE: hum]
[EFFECT] Humidity has a non-monotonic effect. Very low humidity (near 0%) shows some strongly negative values (around −0.5), mid-range humidity (roughly 20–60%) sits slightly above zero (~+0.1), and very high humidity above 80% drives contributions sharply downward, reaching about −0.8 at near-saturation levels. The most favourable humidity is in the moderate range.
[IMPORTANCE] A moderately important feature with a vertical range of about 0.9–1.0 log-units; comparable to month and ranked around third or fourth.

[FEATURE: weathersit]
[EFFECT] Weather acts in steps: clear skies (1) give a small positive boost (~+0.03 to +0.05); mist or cloud (2) is near neutral to slightly negative; light rain or snow (3) strongly suppresses demand, with the bulk of hours falling between −0.15 and −0.65; the very few heavy-rain hours (4) also appear negative (around −0.2).
[IMPORTANCE] A moderate feature with a range of about 0.7 log-units; ranked around sixth or seventh, meaningful mainly because light-rain hours are fairly common.
